text:
maria (People Ops): Quick announcement: launching an on-demand backup caregiving benefit today (partner: NannyNow). Details below, pls read and share. :sparkles:
jordan (Benefits): TL;DR: eligible employees get up to 8 paid backup-care days per 12 months (non-cumulative) to cover unexpected childcare, eldercare, or dependent care. Benefit covers in-home or center care booked through NannyNow or an approved vendor.
olivia (eng): Is this available globally? E.g., will APAC/EU teams be able to use it?
jordan (Benefits): Yes — rolling availability. US & Canada live today; EU & UK live in 2 weeks pending local vendor agreements; APAC available within one month. We'll post region-specific registration links.
marla (People Ops): How do we book?
care-bot: Book via the Redwood Care Portal: https://benefits.redwood/care-backup or call NannyNow 24/7 at +1-800-555-CARE. You must use an approved vendor to be covered.
ta0 (typo)  
(assistant correction) tao (sales): If I use this during planned PTO, does it affect my PTO balance?
jordan (Benefits): Using backup-care days does not deduct from your PTO bank. It's a separate paid day category coded as CGB-2027 in payroll. Managers should mark the day as "backup care" in Workday for visibility.
olivia (eng): What about childcare during business travel?
jordan (Benefits): If travel causes a dependent-care gap (e.g., caregiver unavailable), backup-care can be used while traveling, subject to vendor availability. For international travel, preapproval via Travel Quick Approvals is required — see travel-bot note.
care-bot: Travel Quick Approvals now integrated into mobile: open Redwood App > Travel > Quick Approvals. QR-code boarding approvals will appear for same-day urgent travel.
maria (People Ops): Also: Q3 PTO blackout windows — note small windows for a handful of teams ahead of product launches. This is team-level and will be posted by managers; company-wide blackout is NOT in effect. If you need exceptions, submit: https://forms.redwood/pto-exception and tag your manager.
ta0 (typo again)  
(assistant correction) tao (sales): What documentation is required to submit an exception?
maria (People Ops): Short explanation + manager sign-off. For backup-care related exceptions (e.g., overlapping time off needs), include vendor booking confirmation. We'll aim to respond within 48 hours for exception requests tied to backup care.
olivia (eng): Payroll coding question: will this appear separately on paystubs?
jordan (Benefits): Yes, backup care days will appear as a separate line item coded CGB-2027 with a short descriptor "Backup Care Day". Retroactive adjustments for eligible days taken since Jan 1 will be processed over the next payroll run if you submit receipts by next Friday.
care-bot: FAQ & registration: https://benefits.redwood/care-backup/faq. For urgent help contact benefits@redwood.com.
maria (People Ops): A quick note on conduct while using vendor services: treat vendors with the same code of conduct we expect internally. If you encounter an incident, report to people-ops and security: security@redwood.com.
tao (sales): Appreciate this. One more: are contractors eligible?
jordan (Benefits): Short answer: no, contractors are not eligible for paid backup-care days under this pilot. We will revisit after the pilot period.
maria (People Ops): We're running this as a 6-month pilot; we'll collect usage & satisfaction metrics. Expect a short survey after you register/use the service. Thanks, everyone — questions welcome, ping @maria or @jordan. :heart:
